- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 2–4 days ahead to reflect sentiment direction.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; apply a 2–5% upward bias to counteract pessimism.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
